chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu‘allā ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washshā’, from Abān, from Zurārah, who said:
I heard Abū Ja‘far (عليه السلام) saying: “We are twelve Imams. Among them are Hasan and Husayn, then the Imams are from the offspring of Al-Husayn (عليه السلام).”

key_terms.إِمَامًا: Imam; divinely appointed leader and authority
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةُ: The Imams; the designated successors and leaders
key_terms.الْحُسَيْنِ: Al-Husayn (عليه السلام), from whose progeny the later Imams are
key_terms.اِثْنَا عَشَرَ: Twelve; the stated number of the Imams
key_terms.حَسَنٌ: Al-Hasan (عليه السلام), one of the twelve Imams
key_terms.حُسَيْنٌ: Al-Husayn (عليه السلام), one of the twelve Imams

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the number of the Imams and their lineage?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the divinely appointed leaders are twelve Imams. It identifies Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn (عليهما السلام) among them, and then affirms that the remaining Imams are from the progeny of Al-Husayn (عليه السلام).

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washha, from Aban, from Zurara who said,

‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘We<sup>asws</sup> are twelve Imams<sup>asws</sup>. From them<sup>asws</sup> are Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, and Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, then the Imams<sup>asws</sup> are from the sons<sup>asws</sup> of Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 16. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn mmd from al-Washsha’ from Aban from Zurara who has said the following.
“I heard abu Ja‘far (a.s.) say, ‘We are twelve Imams. Al-Hassan and al-Husayn are of them then are the Imams from the descendants of al-Husayn (a.s.).”
